headline: Divestiture charge masks a steady organic quarter
summary_short: Charles River reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.00B (-2.7% y/y, +0.8% q/q) and a GAAP loss of $(0.03) per diluted share, versus $1.06 EPS a year ago, largely on a $63.7 million divestiture-related charge.
summary_long: Revenue fell 2.7% y/y to $1.00B as May 2026 divestitures (CDMO, Cell Solutions, European Discovery) outweighed 0.1% organic growth, the best since Q3 2023, on higher DSA study volume and Manufacturing's Microbial Solutions growth. GAAP EPS swung to $(0.03) on a $63.7M divestiture loss; non-GAAP EPS fell 3.2% y/y to $3.02 on lower operating margin from higher DSA study costs, partly offset by deferred-compensation gains. GAAP operating margin rose to 11.9% from 9.7% y/y on lower CDMO amortization. CRL repurchased $100M of stock in the quarter; equity fell to $2.84B on buybacks and divestiture losses. FY2026 organic-revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance raised; GAAP EPS guidance lowered to $3.05-$3.35 on divestiture losses.

drivers.explanation: Reported revenue fell as the CDMO, Cell Solutions, and European Discovery divestitures (completed May 2026) outweighed growth; organic revenue (ex-FX/M&A/divestitures) rose 0.1%, the best since Q3 2023, on higher DSA study volume and Manufacturing growth.

The swing to a per-share loss was driven by a $63.7 million loss on the CDMO and Cell Solutions divestiture; non-GAAP EPS separately fell 3.2% y/y on lower operating margin, partly offset by deferred-compensation investment gains.
GAAP operating margin rose to 11.9% from 9.7% y/y, primarily on lower accelerated amortization tied to certain client relationships in the CDMO business.
The net loss was driven by the $63.7 million CDMO/Cell Solutions divestiture loss and a higher tax provision, which outweighed the y/y improvement in operating income.

Cash was roughly flat q/q: $220.8 million of six-month operating cash flow was largely offset by $379.7 million of investing outflows, including a $467.3 million acquisition, and treasury-stock buybacks.
Equity declined primarily on $323.2 million of treasury stock repurchased under the buyback program plus lower retained earnings following divestiture-related losses.

FY2026 organic-revenue guidance raised to 0.0%-1.0% (from -1.5% to -0.5%) and non-GAAP EPS guidance raised to $11.15-$11.45 (from $10.80-$11.30) on improving DSA demand and stronger Manufacturing results; GAAP EPS guidance lowered to $3.05-$3.35 on divestiture losses.
